newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey hosts Moslem nations' ministerial meeting.
newsitem.headline: Turkey hosts Moslem nations' ministerial meeting.

text.p: Turkey's Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan on Saturday opened a meeting of high-level officials from eight Moslem countries in Istanbul aimed at boosting economic cooperation among them.
Ministers from Turkey, Egypt, Iran, Pakistan, Nigeria, Bangladesh, Malaysia and Indonesia gathered in the city to discuss a possible summit between their leaders later this year.
"Our aim is for this meeting to be profitable not just for these countries, but for all humanity," Erbakan said in a speech at the start of the one-day talks.

Erbakan has visited all the participating countries, except Bangladesh, since coming to power in June. During that time he has given priority to strengthening secular, but Moslem, Turkey's links with the Islamic world.
These moves have been a source of friction between Erbakan and NATO-member Turkey's western allies, notably the United States.

In December, Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani made a visit to Turkey which drew criticism from the United States. Washington was also annoyed by a $23 billion agreement which Turkey signed in August for the supply of Iranian natural gas over 23 years.
Saturday's talks could prepare the way for a summit of the eight countries' leaders in the first quarter of 1997, Turkish foreign ministry officials have said.

Preparatory work on the organisation, known as D-8 and to be based in Istanbul, began last year following Erbakan's foreign trips. Officials previously met in November to discuss the group's development.
The foreign ministers of Iran and Pakistan will also hold a trilateral meeting with Turkish officials on Sunday to discuss the situation in Afghanistan.
